projects.title: Autonomous Parking Spot Detection Drone
projects.description: Built a drone system using Infineon PSoC 6 and Raspberry Pi to autonomously detect empty parking spots using radar sensing and computer vision.

Excited to wrap up my summer 2026 internship at the Scalable and Ubiquitous Networking Lab (Sun Lab) at University of Georgia. Over the past 2 months, I worked on RadioLens, an extended reality (XR) system for measuring, visualizing, and modeling wireless networks in physical spaces. I built across the stack: from collecting spatial Wi-Fi measurements on a Meta Quest 3 and developing mixed-reality visualizations to integrating ray-tracing models for analysis and optimization. Along the way, I learned a ton about building real world software systems at the intersection of XR, computer vision, machine learning, human-computer-interaction, and had the opportunity to contribute to our paper on the system. Massive thanks to Professor Haijian Sun , Professor Zhenlin An , and the rest of the SunLab team who helped me along the way. Pictured below is the RadioLens system overview.

Over the past few months, I’ve been thinking a lot about the people and experiences that made my time at the University of California, Berkeley so meaningful. In May, I graduated with a B.A. in Psychology, along with minors in Global Poverty & Practice and Public Policy. I'm so thankful for the professors, mentors, and peers who challenged me, supported me, and helped shape both my personal and professional growth at Berkeley. A special thank you to Dr. Colette Auerswald for her mentorship and encouragement, and to Tessa Stapp and the entire Youth & Allies Against Homelessness (YAAH) Lab for their dedication to ending youth homelessness through community-engaged research. Thank you as well to my incredible Youth Equity Discovery Initiative (YEDI) mentors, Marieka Schotland, Ph.D. , Dr. Amia Nash Chambers , Paula S. Nordstrom Miranda, MS , and Evelyn Riley , for fostering such a supportive community and showing me what equitable, youth-centered leadership truly looks like. I'm also grateful to the amazing team at UC Berkeley's PATH to Care Center, where I had the opportunity to support survivor-centered services while contributing to research addressing the intersection of sexual violence and student homelessness. This experience strengthened my commitment to trauma-informed, compassionate, and equity-driven work. The Global Poverty & Practice minor provided me invaluable opportunities to connect classroom learning with community-engaged practice. Through coursework and the practicum I completed last summer at Solid Ground , I developed a deeper understanding of the structural causes of poverty and homelessness, which continue to shape how I approach this work. I'm excited to share that I've accepted a full-time position at Solid Ground as the Administrative Services & Referral Coordinator. I'm grateful for the opportunity to return to Solid Ground and continue supporting our community, connecting people with critical resources, and learning alongside such a dedicated team. Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey. I'm excited for this next chapter and look forward to continuing to grow as a researcher, advocate, and community partner!

Excited to share that I completed Break Through Tech AI’s 9-week Machine Learning Foundations course from Cornell University through eCornell and earned my certificate. The program focused on applying machine learning to real-world problems and preparing fellows for industry AI projects. Along the way, I strengthened my foundation in data preparation, model training, and evaluation using Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and Keras. I also went beyond traditional ML by building a RAG chatbot and an MCP tool, which gave me hands-on experience connecting language models with external knowledge and tools. Grateful for everything I learned and excited to keep building more practical AI systems. https://lnkd.in/ey3B7XQN #BreakThroughTechAI #MachineLearning #ArtificialIntelligence #RAG #MCP #CornellTech
